perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s perspective, his available information is:

- I am Bradley Ochoa, a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager. We work together professionally and sometimes disagree about sales versus marketing strategy.
- In a meeting room, I prepared data and charts to support traditional sales techniques. I believed our core sales would benefit more from traditional methods and felt those proven methods were being sidelined for newer digital strategies Katherine supports.
- I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed traditional methods deserved more consideration. I heard her say she saw my point, but that the market is evolving, digital outreach cannot be ignored, and she asked how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement rates.
- I replied that I was not suggesting abandoning digital marketing, but was frustrated that proven methods were being sidelined without proper consideration. I heard Katherine say she understood my frustration, that it is about balance, and that we should analyze the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital-campaign success stories that had significantly boosted engagement and sales. I began to question my support for only traditional methods and asked her to explain how those strategies are developed.
- I heard Katherine explain that it is about targeting the right audience with the right message, and she offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making behind a recent campaign.
- I admitted I had doubts about moving away from traditional methods, but seeing the outcomes made me want to understand digital more. I heard her say she was glad I was open, that adapting to market trends matters, and that we should dive deeper into the data.
- I proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital strategies. I heard Katherine agree and suggest scheduling time to brainstorm and outline next steps. I said I was hopeful we could leverage both our expertise and appreciated her willingness to collaborate. I heard her say she looked forward to it and wanted to leverage each other’s strengths.
- After the joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime to prepare a board presentation showcasing the integrated approach. I told Katherine I had a draft integrating both our ideas. I heard her say it looked comprehensive and well thought out and that my hard work showed. I thanked her and said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors. I heard her say she was confident and suggested reviewing and fine-tuning it once more.
- After the presentation and implementation of the new strategy, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our successful collaboration. I thanked Katherine, said I had learned much from her, and proposed regular strategy sessions. I heard her say it had been a pleasure, that my openness made the partnership successful, and that regular sessions were a fantastic idea to stay on top of our game and market trends.
